chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man upon whom death was approaching, so he freed his slave, who was his only property. The heirs refused to approve of that. He asked: What is the ruling in this matter? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Only one-third of him is freed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dying man frees his only slave and the heirs disagree?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of a sole asset during the final illness (*marad al-mawt*) by ruling that only one-third of the slave's value is subject to the testator's discretion for emancipation, while the remaining two-thirds are reserved for the heirs. This ruling aligns with the general principle of *wasiyya* (bequest) in Islamic jurisprudence, ensuring that the heirs' rights are preserved even when the deceased wishes to free a single dependent slave. The context highlights the balance between the deceased's charitable intent and the financial security of the surviving family.
